title: Harden the monorepo foundation for AI-led production development
objective: Make the repository safe and reproducible for AI-led development by enforcing task scope in clean CI checkouts, rejecting type-safety escapes, pinning and auditing the toolchain, validating Cloudflare deployment configuration, using generated Worker bindings with runtime environment validation, and covering recovery, persistence, and security-sensitive rejection paths with tests.
constraints: AGENTS.mdの規約と既存の依存方向を維持する
明示的な型安全性の回避や未検証の外部入力を追加しない
ゲームルールとプロトコル互換性を変更しない
実在するCloudflare resource IDや秘密情報を仮定しない
既存のローカル、staging、production分離を維持する

acceptanceCriteria.description: AI task scope is enforced for both uncommitted work and committed CI diffs, and the harness self-test proves allowed, forbidden, renamed, base-ref, malformed-task, and deleted-task cases
Explicit any types, TypeScript suppression directives, and double-cast assertions are rejected, with all existing unsafe double casts removed
The pinned dependency graph installs with an explicit install-script allowlist, has no high-severity audit finding, and satisfies npm dependency integrity

Cloudflare bindings come from Wrangler-generated types, runtime environment values are validated, and staging or production deployment fails before side effects when placeholders, local auth, secrets, or client IDs are invalid
acceptanceCriteria.verification: npm run test --workspace @discord-hero/activity && npm run test:deployment-preflight

acceptanceCriteria.description: Durable Object hibernation restores room identity, related player persistence writes are batched, and request or WebSocket logs do not include raw room paths or close reasons
Repository formatting, lint, typecheck, tests, build, local migration, and AI verification all pass with a reviewed verification report

notes: The task intentionally covers repository harness, CI, dependency policy, Worker boundary validation, and deployment preflight because they jointly determine whether future AI-authored changes can be trusted. Placeholder production resource values remain configuration inputs; the new preflight must reject them rather than fabricate replacements.
